title.en: Single-qubit pure and mixed states on the Bloch ball

summary: Relate a single-qubit density matrix to a point in the Bloch ball and distinguish pure-state phase from statistical mixing.
objective: Drag a valid Bloch vector and compare density-matrix entries, purity and computational-basis probabilities.
intent_signals: Drag a valid Bloch vector and compare density-matrix entries, purity and computational-basis probabilities.
Relate a single-qubit density matrix to a point in the Bloch ball and distinguish pure-state phase from statistical mixing.
example_prompts: Build an explorable single-qubit pure and mixed states on the bloch ball. Drag a valid Bloch vector and compare density-matrix entries, purity and computational-basis probabilities.

entities.name: State sphere and vector
entities.guidance: Draw a unit sphere with labeled +X,+Y,+Z axes and six basis reference points. The vector tip may lie inside; its length is a state-space quantity, not a spatial electron location.

entities.name: Density matrix tiles
entities.guidance: Display rho=1/2[[1+rz,rx-i*ry],[rx+i*ry,1-rz]] with separately labeled real and imaginary tiles. Link a selected component to its Bloch axis without projecting complex entries onto arbitrary heights.

entities.name: Pure-state chart and mixture chord
entities.guidance: At unit radius show |psi>=cos(theta/2)|0>+exp(i*phi)sin(theta/2)|1>, theta polar from+Z and phi azimuth from+X toward+Y. For a mixture of two chosen pure endpoints, show the chord point p*rA+(1-p)*rB and weightp; interior points have no single pure ket.

state_contract.model: Authoritative real r=(rx,ry,rz) satisfies |r|<=1; reject invalid numeric edits rather than silently changing them. rho=(I+r dot sigma)/2 in the stated Pauli convention. Derived eigenvalues=(1+|r|)/2,(1-|r|)/2; purity=(1+|r|^2)/2; P0=(1+rz)/2,P1=(1-rz)/2. Mixture p in[0,1] is a convex combination of density matrices, not a coherent amplitude sum.
state_contract.authority: Bloch vector or an explicitly selected two-endpoint mixture owns rho and readouts. For pure chart coordinates r=(sin theta cos phi,sin theta sin phi,cos theta); at poles azimuth is irrelevant, and at r=0 direction is undefined. Camera rotation never changes the state.
actions: Select |0>,|1>,|+>,|->,|+i>,|-i> or the maximally mixed state.
Edit r with a validity indicator, or move a handle restricted to the ball.
Vary mixture weight and compare different ensembles giving the same rho.
Toggle a pure-state global phase display: rho, Bloch point and probabilities stay unchanged.
Reset vector, mixture endpoints/weight and chart selections; pause any demonstration animation without changing the state.

invariants: rho is Hermitian with trace1 and nonnegative eigenvalues within declared numerical tolerance.
Pure states have |r|=1 and purity1; r=0 gives rho=I/2, purity1/2 and no unique direction.
The equal mixture of opposite poles and equal mixture of opposite X states both yield r=0; neither equals the pure |+> state.
Computational-basis probabilities sum to1; changing pure-state azimuth at fixed theta leaves them unchanged but changes other-axis components away from poles.
motion_guidance: Any animated route is an explicitly authored state-preparation or mixture sweep; do not call a straight interior chord unitary evolution.
At poles retain a harmless UI azimuth choice but mark it nonunique. Hide directional arrowhead at zero rather than normalizing zero.
known_limits: One qubit only; the ball does not represent the full joint state or entanglement of multiple qubits, nor an electron orbit or wavefunction in physical space.
No hardware execution, measurement sample generator, noise channel or calibrated quantum-control pulse is supplied. Mixture decompositions are not generally unique.
Authored recipe and prospective checks only; no runtime artifact or rendered result has been observed.

claims.statement: For one qubit, pure states up to global phase correspond to unit Bloch vectors with coordinates(sin theta cos phi,sin theta sin phi,cos theta) in the Pauli decomposition rho=(I+r dot sigma)/2. Convex mixtures give points inside the ball, including the maximally mixed state I/2 at its center.
claims.scope: One qubit, normalized density matrices, conventional Pauli axes, global-phase equivalence and mixtures; not electron position.

source_refs.locator: Qubit states as points on a sphere; Pauli decomposition; Six important examples; Convex combinations of points

object_craft.family: Single-qubit pure and mixed states on the Bloch ball
object_craft.structure: Make the sphere, vector, six reference pins, mixture chord and matrix panel separate objects with one shared state identity. Labels carry ket signs and i explicitly, not only hue.
object_craft.material: Use independent line weights, shapes and labels for mathematical roles. Color and surface finish are presentation choices; do not infer material physics from them.

creative_affordances: A minimal geometric instrument or a translucent teaching sculpture can share the same density-matrix contract; the matrix and probability panels may remain planar for readability.

physical_contract.scope: Derived mathematical geometry and authored inspection; no contact dynamics or calibrated physical artifact.
checks: rho is Hermitian with trace1 and nonnegative eigenvalues within declared numerical tolerance.
Pure states have |r|=1 and purity1; r=0 gives rho=I/2, purity1/2 and no unique direction.
